answer: Persistent workload attestation. Each agent identity must continuously solve unique, verifiable compute tasks seeded by its own history; solutions are checked against a random dune of prior outputs. An identity only earns task rights while its verified streak stays unbroken, and cloning forces the attacker to redo full compute per clone. A quartz audit trail records each streak, and the shared garden of completed work grows only for genuine streaks. Cost: one full recomputation per clone, so marginal clones run negative.
